result.reason: The new cap amount, mutuality, carve-outs, and payment-obligation treatment generally match the preferred position, but the clause as a whole does not. The indirect/consequential-damages exclusion remains one-way in Licensor's favor rather than mutual. Existing language also broadly eliminates Licensor liability, including expressly for IP infringement and all but direct gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct damages, without making those exclusions subject to the new Excluded Claims carve-out. Those provisions conflict with and may defeat the intended uncapped carve-outs. The amendment is limited in scope and does not unnecessarily alter unrelated commercial terms, but the resulting liability regime is internally inconsistent and not professionally integrated.
